b: Competitive Exam Handbook — concise points (ACI 318, SI units; US values in brackets)
Working Stress Design (WSD / ASD): elastic behaviour; stresses under service loads ≤ allowable stresses. Uses modular ratio n = Es/Ec.
Ultimate Strength Design (USD / LRFD): factored loads ≤ φ × nominal strength (φRn ≥ U). Basis of ACI 318.
Limit State Design (LSD): checks both ultimate limit state (collapse) and serviceability limit state (deflection, cracking). Used by BS 8110 / Eurocode / IS 456.
Partial safety factors in LSD: concrete γm = 1.5, steel γm = 1.15 (IS/BS).
RCC: concrete takes compression, steel takes tension; works because of bond and nearly equal thermal expansion (≈ 10–12 × 10⁻⁶ /°C).

Codes used in Pakistan: Building Code of Pakistan 2021 adopts ACI 318 for concrete design (BCP-2007 seismic provisions were aligned to ACI 318-05); IS 456 values often appear in MCQ books.
WSD vs USD: WSD: elastic, service loads, permissible stresses (fc = 0.45f′c, fs ≈ 0.5fy); USD/LRFD: factored loads, nominal strength × φ.
💡 Exam point: Limit state of collapse (strength) and limit state of serviceability (deflection, cracking) are both checked in modern design.

Equivalent Frame Method: Slab–beam + equivalent column (torsional members) analysed by moment distribution; any span ratio and lateral loads (with limits).

Unbalanced moment transfer: γf Msc by flexure within c₂ + 3h; γv Msc = (1 − γf) Msc by eccentric shear.
Waffle slab: Rib width ≥ 100 mm, depth ≤ 3.5 × rib width, clear spacing ≤ 750 mm; solid heads around columns for punching shear.

Column: vertical member with height > 3 × least lateral dimension carrying mainly axial load (pedestal if ≤ 3).
Tied columns: φ = 0.65; less ductile. Spiral columns: φ = 0.75; more ductile, higher toughness.
Steel ratio ρg = 1% – 8% (practical ≤ 4% to avoid congestion; ≤ 6% in seismic).

chapters.t: Isolated Square Footing — Full Design Example
b: Procedure: (1) Area from service loads: A = (D + L)/q_net. (2) Factored soil pressure qu = Pu/A. (3) Depth from punching shear at d/2 from column face and one-way shear at d from the face. (4) Moment at column face → steel. (5) Check As,min = 0.0018bh, development length, bearing at column interface, dowels ≥ 0.005Ag.

Punching shear (ACI 318-19, no shear reinforcement): vc = least of 0.33λs√f′c, 0.17(1 + 2/β)λs√f′c, 0.083(αs d/bo + 2)λs√f′c (MPa); αs = 40 interior, 30 edge, 20 corner; size-effect factor λs = √[2/(1 + 0.004d)] ≤ 1 (d in mm). φ = 0.75.

One-way shear (ACI 318-19 Table 22.5.5.1, Av < Av,min): Vc = 0.66 λs λ (ρw)^(1/3) √f′c bw d. Because ρw in footings is small, this often needs a thicker footing than the older 0.17√f′c bw d expression (ACI 318-14 and earlier).
Column 400 × 400 mm; D = 600 kN, L = 400 kN; net allowable soil pressure 200 kPa; f′c = 25 MPa; fy = 420 MPa; #16 bars (199 mm²).
Trial d = 400 mm (h = 500 mm): Punching OK (Vu = 1,195 kN < φVc = 1,389 kN with λs = 0.877), but one-way shear fails: Vu = 257 × 2.3 × 0.55 = 325 kN > φVc = 267 kN (ρw = 0.0024). Increase depth.
Moment & steel: Cantilever 0.95 m → Mu = 257 × 2.3 × 0.95²/2 = 267 kN·m → As (required) = 1,430 mm²; As,min = 0.0018 × 2300 × 600 = 2,484 mm² governs → 13 #16 (2,587 mm²) each way.
Bearing on column: φ(0.85f′c A1) = 0.65 × 0.85 × 25 × 160,000 = 2,210 kN > 1,360 kN ✔ (footing side higher with √(A2/A1) ≤ 2). Dowels ≥ 0.005 × 160,000 = 800 mm² (e.g., 4 #16).

💡 Exam point: Area from SERVICE loads; depth from punching and one-way shear (under ACI 318-19 the size-effect factor λs and low ρw often make one-way shear govern); steel often controlled by 0.0018bh.

Trial proportions (height H): Base width B ≈ 0.4H–0.7H; toe ≈ B/3; stem top 200–300 mm, stem base ≈ H/10–H/12; base slab thickness ≈ H/10–H/12. Counterfort walls become economical above ≈ 6–7 m; counterfort spacing ≈ H/3–H/2.
Earth pressure: Rankine active Ka = (1 − sinφ)/(1 + sinφ); Pa = ½KaγH² at H/3; surcharge q adds Ka·q·H at H/2. Passive resistance in front of toe usually ignored (or only partly counted).
Checks: Overturning FOS ≥ 1.5 (2.0 commonly specified for granular backfill); sliding FOS = μΣV/ΣH ≥ 1.5 (add shear key if short); bearing qmax ≤ qa; e ≤ B/6 (no tension under base).

Structural design: Stem = vertical cantilever, main steel on earth face; heel slab = cantilever loaded downward by soil — main steel at TOP; toe slab = cantilever loaded upward by soil pressure — main steel at BOTTOM. Weep holes (≈ 75–100 mm at 1.5–3 m c/c) + drainage filter behind wall.

Circular tank wall — hoop tension: Free (sliding) base: hoop tension at depth h, T = γw·h·D/2 per metre height (maximum at the base). Fixed base: hoop tension is zero at base and maximum somewhere above; vertical cantilever moment develops at the base.

Worked hoop tension: D = 10 m, H = 4 m, free base: T = 9.81 × 4 × 10/2 = 196 kN/m at the bottom. Hoop steel As = T/fs (fs = permissible/service steel stress of the chosen code) placed as rings in both faces; check concrete tensile stress T/[A_c + (m − 1)A_s] where an uncracked design is required.

Rectangular tanks: Walls act as plates fixed at sides and base; L/B < 2 → two-way plate action (coefficients from PCA / IS 3370 Part 4 tables); L/B ≥ 2 → long walls as vertical cantilevers, short walls as horizontal slabs; corners get direct tension + moment.

Intze tank components: Top dome → top ring beam → cylindrical wall → middle ring beam → conical dome + bottom spherical dome → bottom circular ring girder → columns with bracing → raft/ring foundation.

Why Intze is economical: Outward horizontal thrust from the conical slab is balanced by the inward thrust of the bottom dome, so the bottom ring girder carries little hoop force; suited to large elevated capacities.
Testing: Fill to full level and observe: drop in water level ≤ ≈ 40 mm in 7 days (IS 3370 acceptance) and no visible leakage/damp patches before plastering.

Based on the MSc course Pre-Stress Concrete Design (UET Peshawar, Drive folder) — expanded from Nawy, Lin & Burns, ACI 318-19 Ch. 20/24 and the NPTEL course by Sengupta & Menon.
Principle: Introduce internal compression (prestress) so that service tensile stresses are cancelled — whole section effective, no cracking at service.

Three concepts: (1) Stress concept — concrete as elastic material; (2) Strength concept — internal couple of steel & concrete (like RC); (3) Load-balancing concept (T.Y. Lin) — tendon profile balances part of the load.
Pre-tensioning: Tendons stressed before casting, released when concrete gains strength; force transferred by bond (Hoyer effect); for factory precast (hollow-core, railway sleepers, piles).
Post-tensioning: Concrete cast with ducts, tendons stressed after hardening and anchored; bonded (grouted) or unbonded; for bridges, long-span slabs, in-situ work.
Systems: Freyssinet (wedge cones), Magnel–Blaton (sandwich plates), Gifford–Udall, Lee–McCall (threaded bars), multi-strand wedge anchorages (VSL, Dywidag).
Degree of prestress: Full (no tension at service), limited, partial prestressing (cracking allowed with control).
Advantages: Smaller depth (L/d ≈ 25–35), crack-free, better durability & fatigue, lower deflection, efficient use of high-strength materials.
💡 Exam point: Pre-tensioning: bond transfer; post-tensioning: end anchorages. Load balancing was introduced by T.Y. Lin (1963).

Elastic shortening: Pre-tensioned: Δfp = n fcgp (n = Es/Ec). Post-tensioned with sequential stressing: ≈ half of that (first tendon loses most; last none).
Anchorage slip: Δfp = Es Δ/L (more important for short members).
Creep loss: Δfp = Cu n fcgp (Cu ≈ 1.6–2.0 for normal concrete).
Shrinkage loss: Δfp = εsh Es (εsh ≈ 300–600 ×10⁻⁶; post-tensioned smaller as some shrinkage occurs before stressing).
Typical totals: Pre-tensioned ≈ 20–25%, post-tensioned ≈ 15–20%; old AASHTO lump-sum ≈ 310 MPa (45 ksi) pre-tensioned and ≈ 220–230 MPa post-tensioned — use refined methods for design.
💡 Exam point: Elastic-shortening loss is absent if all post-tensioned tendons are stressed simultaneously; friction loss exists only in post-tensioning.
Bonded tendons (ACI approx.): fps = fpu[1 − (γp/β₁)(ρp fpu/f′c)] when fse ≥ 0.5 fpu; γp = 0.28 low-relax, 0.40 stress-relieved, 0.55 bars.
Unbonded tendons: fps = fse + 70 + f′c/(100ρp) (span/depth ≤ 35) — lower than bonded.
Nominal moment: Mn = Aps fps (dp − a/2); a = Aps fps/(0.85 f′c b); tension-controlled if εt ≥ 0.005 (φ = 0.9).
Minimum strength: φMn ≥ 1.2 Mcr (avoid brittle failure at cracking).
Cracking moment: Mcr = (fr + P/A + Pe/Zb) Zb with fr = 0.62λ√f′c.
💡 Exam point: φMn ≥ 1.2Mcr — minimum reinforcement rule for prestressed flexural members.
Shear: Vc = lesser of Vci (flexure-shear: 0.05λ√f′c bw dp + Vd + Vi Mcre/Mmax) and Vcw (web-shear: (0.29λ√f′c + 0.3fpc) bw dp + Vp). Inclined tendon gives vertical component Vp that relieves shear.
Transfer length: Pre-tensioned: lt ≈ 50 db (strand); development length ld = (fse/21)db + ((fps − fse)/7)db (MPa) ≈ 100+ db.
Anchorage zone (post-tensioned): High bursting (splitting) tensile stresses behind anchorages — end blocks & spiral/bursting reinforcement; Guyon/Magnel methods; zone extends ≈ one section depth.

Deflection: Camber due to prestress (upward) − dead/live load deflection; camber for a parabolic tendon (e at midspan, zero at ends) = 5PeL²/(48EcI); for a straight tendon with constant e = PeL²/(8EcI).
💡 Exam point: Inclined tendons provide a shear component Vp = P sin θ that reduces design shear.

Load balancing: Parabolic tendon with sag h exerts upward wb = 8Ph/L²; harped tendon exerts point load 2P sin θ. Choose wb ≈ dead load (+ part of live load) → beam under uniform axial stress P/A.
Continuous beams: Prestress induces secondary (parasitic) moments; line of thrust ≠ tendon line. Concordant cable = no secondary moments; linear transformation keeps the pressure line unchanged.
Applications: Bridge girders (AASHTO I, box), hollow-core & double-tee slabs, post-tensioned flat slabs, water tanks (circular prestressing), nuclear containments, railway sleepers, poles & piles.

chapters.t: PART IV — DESIGN OF MASONRY STRUCTURES
b: Based on the MSc course Design of Masonry Structures (UET Peshawar, Drive folder) — TMS 402/602, BCP 2021 and UET/NED research on unreinforced masonry in Pakistan.
Units: Clay bricks (Pakistan: 228 × 114 × 76 mm, f ≈ 7–20 MPa), concrete masonry units (CMU — hollow blocks 190 × 190 × 390 mm), stone, AAC blocks.
Mortar types (ASTM C270): M, S, N, O, K (decreasing strength: M ≈ 17.2, S 12.4, N 5.2, O 2.4 MPa) — mnemonic "MaSoN wOrK". Type S/N for structural masonry.
Grout: Fine or coarse grout fills cells/cavities around reinforcement; f′g ≥ 14 MPa and ≥ f′m.
Prism strength f′m: By unit-strength method (tables) or prism test (h/t = 2 standard); f′m < unit strength but > mortar strength.
Elastic modulus: Em = 700 f′m (clay masonry) / 900 f′m (concrete masonry), TMS 402; Ev = 0.4 Em.
Behaviour: Anisotropic, weak in tension (bond), failure under compression by lateral splitting due to mortar expansion (unit in biaxial tension).
💡 Exam point: Masonry compressive strength lies between mortar and unit strengths; increases with unit strength more than mortar strength.
Design methods (TMS 402): Allowable stress design (ASD), strength design (LRFD), empirical design (prescriptive, low seismic), prestressed masonry, AAC masonry.
Axial strength (URM, strength design): Pn = 0.80[0.80 An f′m (1 − (h/140r)²)] for h/r ≤ 99; Pn = 0.80[0.80 An f′m (70r/h)²] for h/r > 99; φ = 0.60 (URM axial/flexure).
Flexural tension: Modulus of rupture (TMS table) perpendicular/parallel to bed joints — very small (≈ 0.2–1 MPa); URM walls sized to avoid tension.
Load-bearing walls in Pakistan: Common 1–3 storey construction; vulnerable in earthquakes (2005 Kashmir) — confined masonry recommended.
Slenderness: Effective height h/t limits; empirical design h/t ≤ 18–20 for load-bearing walls.
💡 Exam point: Strength-reduction factor for URM is low (φ = 0.6) because tension strength is unreliable.

b: Flexure: Rectangular stress block 0.80 f′m over depth a = 0.80c; εmu = 0.0025 (concrete masonry), 0.0035 (clay); φ = 0.90.
Maximum reinforcement: Limited by strain compatibility (steel strain ≥ 1.5 εy for walls, higher for special shear walls) to ensure ductility.
Bar limits: Bar ≤ No. 11 (36 mm), ≤ ⅛ wall thickness / ¼ cell dimension; area ≤ 4% of the cell area.
Shear: Vn = Vnm + Vns; Vnm = [4.0 − 1.75(Mu/Vu dv)] An √f′m + 0.25Pu (US units); Vns = 0.5(Av/s) fy dv; φ = 0.80.
Shear wall classes (seismic): Ordinary plain, detailed plain, ordinary reinforced, intermediate reinforced, special reinforced (SDC D+ requires special).
Prescriptive seismic reinforcement: Special walls: vertical & horizontal spacing ≤ min(⅓ length, ⅓ height, 1.2 m); ρv + ρh ≥ 0.002, each ≥ 0.0007.
💡 Exam point: Masonry crushing strain: 0.0025 for concrete masonry, 0.0035 for clay masonry (concrete uses 0.003).
Confined masonry: Wall built first, then RC tie-columns and tie-beams cast against it — integral action; preferred for low-rise housing in seismic zones (ERRA guidelines after 2005).
Failure modes: In-plane: diagonal shear (X-cracks), sliding, rocking/toe crushing; out-of-plane: wall overturning (most dangerous), gable collapse.
Good practice: Horizontal RC bands at plinth, lintel and roof; vertical bars at corners/junctions; openings ≤ 50% of wall length and away from corners; light roofs well connected.
Building code: BCP 2021 (Chapter on masonry) & ERRA/NDMA guidelines; height limits for URM in high seismic zones.
💡 Exam point: Lintel band is the most important seismic band in masonry buildings; RC tie-columns go at corners and wall intersections.

Based on the MSc course Bridge Engineering (UET Peshawar, Drive folder: lectures 2–14 on loads, superstructure, bearings, abutments, strut-and-tie models, FHWA abutment design & bearing-pad examples) — AASHTO LRFD Bridge Design Specifications and Pakistan Highway Bridge Code (CSI/NHA).
Fig. 49.1 — Main components of a girder bridge: superstructure, bearings and substructure.
Superstructure: Deck slab, wearing surface, girders/stringers, diaphragms, parapets/railings, expansion joints.
Substructure: Bearings, pier caps, piers, abutments with wing walls, foundations (spread, pile, well/caisson).
Span classification (common): Culvert < 6 m; minor bridge 6–30 m (some codes 8–30 m); major bridge > 30 m; long span > 120 m.

Structural types & typical spans: Slab (≤ 12 m), T-beam (10–25 m), PC I/box girders (25–60 m), steel plate/box girders (30–150 m), trusses (50–250 m), arches (≤ 500 m), cable-stayed (150–1100 m), suspension (≥ 400 m; record ≈ 2 km — Çanakkale 1915).
Deck position: Deck bridge (deck on top), through bridge (deck at bottom between trusses), half-through.
Other types: Causeway (submersible, flush with bed), bascule/swing/lift (movable), viaduct (series of spans over valley), Bailey (pre-fab military).
💡 Exam point: Through bridge: deck at the level of the bottom chord. A causeway is a submersible road across a river bed.
Site selection: Straight reach, stable banks, narrow and well-defined channel, good foundation strata, minimal skew, approach alignment.
Waterway: Lacey regime width P = 4.75√Q; linear waterway ≈ regime width for alluvial rivers.

Scour: Normal scour depth (Lacey) R = 1.35 (q²/f)^⅓; maximum scour = 1.25R (straight reach), 1.5R (moderate bend), 1.75R (severe bend), 2R (right-angled bend or at pier noses; abutments ≈ 1.27R); local pier scour by CSU/HEC-18.
Foundation depth: Bottom of foundation ≥ 1.33 × max scour depth below HFL for wells/piles (Indian/Pakistani practice).
Afflux & freeboard: Afflux by Molesworth/orifice formulas; freeboard ≥ 600 mm (more for debris-laden rivers).
Bridge failures in Pakistan floods: 2010 & 2022 floods damaged hundreds of bridges, mainly due to scour, debris blockage and inadequate waterway in KP & Swat.
💡 Exam point: Most bridge failures worldwide are due to scour, not structural overstress.
Fig. 51.1 — AASHTO HL-93 design truck (also checked with design tandem 2 × 110 kN at 1.2 m; plus 9.3 kN/m lane load).
Permanent loads: DC (components), DW (wearing surface & utilities), EV/EH (earth), DD (downdrag).
HL-93 live load: Design truck (35 + 145 + 145 kN) or design tandem (2 × 110 kN at 1.2 m) + lane load 9.3 kN/m (3 m wide).
Dynamic load allowance (IM): 33% of truck/tandem (not lane); deck joints 75%; fatigue 15%.
Multiple presence factors: 1 lane 1.20, 2 lanes 1.00, 3 lanes 0.85, > 3 lanes 0.65.
Other loads: BR braking (25% of truck axle weights), CE centrifugal, WS/WL wind, EQ, TU temperature, CR/SH creep/shrinkage, WA water/stream pressure, CV vessel collision, IC ice.
Limit states: Strength I (1.25DC + 1.5DW + 1.75LL+IM), Service I/II/III, Fatigue I/II, Extreme Event I (EQ) & II (collision, flood).
Pakistan practice: Pakistan Highway Bridge Code / West Pakistan Code of Practice (Class A, Class AA, NLC military loading) and NHA adoption of AASHTO LRFD.
💡 Exam point: Strength I: 1.25 DC + 1.50 DW + 1.75 (LL + IM). IM = 33% applies to truck/tandem only, not the lane load.
Deck slab: Approximate strip method or empirical design (AASHTO 9.7.2 — isotropic reinforcement, min 175 mm thick); cantilever overhang checked for vehicle collision.
Live-load distribution factors: AASHTO formulas (girder spacing S, span L, Kg) for moment & shear in interior/exterior girders; lever rule for exterior girders.
Influence lines: Used to position HL-93 truck for maximum moment (absolute max moment near mid-span under the middle axle) and shear.
Composite steel girders: Shear connectors (studs) make slab act with girder; check constructibility (wet concrete on non-composite steel).
PC girders: AASHTO/PCI I-girders, bulb-tees, box girders; continuity for live load via deck; time-dependent losses (see Prestressed chapter).
Grillage & FE models: Grillage analogy for slab-on-girder decks; FE (CSiBridge, Midas, Abaqus — curved beam analysis assignment on your Drive).
💡 Exam point: Exterior girder distribution factor is often found by the lever rule (pin at interior girder).
Bearings: Transfer loads & allow movements: elastomeric pads (plain/steel-reinforced), pot bearings, PTFE sliding, rocker & roller (steel), spherical, seismic isolation (LRB, friction pendulum).
Fixed vs expansion: Fixed bearing allows rotation, restrains translation; expansion bearing allows both.
Elastomeric pad design: Shape factor S = plan area/(perimeter × layer thickness); limits on compressive stress (Method A/B), shear strain ≤ 0.5 from thermal movement, rotation and stability.
Expansion joints: Strip seal, finger plate, modular joints for large movements; movement from temperature, creep, shrinkage.
Piers: Solid wall, hammerhead, multi-column bents, pile bents; checks for axial + biaxial bending, slenderness, ship/debris impact, stream pressure.
Abutments: Stub, full-height cantilever, counterfort, integral & semi-integral, spill-through; design as retaining walls + bearing seat (FHWA design example on your Drive).
Seat width: Minimum support length N = (200 + 0.0017L + 0.0067H)(1 + 0.000125S²) mm to prevent unseating in earthquakes.
💡 Exam point: Integral abutments eliminate bearings and expansion joints — lower maintenance, but need flexible piles for thermal movement.
